ai.subject: Anatomy
ai.summary: The autonomic nervous system (ANS) is a hidden network that regulates involuntary organs. It balances sympathetic and parasympathetic signals to keep heart, lungs, gut and glands in sync. Understanding its pathways helps diagnose and treat life‑threatening dysregulation.

sections.p: The ANS is a division of the peripheral nervous system that controls involuntary functions. It operates through two complementary branches: sympathetic (fight‑or‑flight) and parasympathetic (rest‑and‑digest).
b: Sympathetic increases heart rate, dilates pupils, inhibits digestion
Parasympathetic slows heart, constricts pupils, stimulates digestion

sections.p: Sympathetic pre‑ganglionic neurons originate in the thoracolumbar spinal cord (T1–L2). Parasympathetic pre‑ganglionic neurons arise from the brainstem (cranial nerves III, VII, IX, X) and sacral spinal cord (S2–S4).
b: Sympathetic ganglia are near the spinal cord (paravertebral and prevertebral)
Parasympathetic ganglia are close to target organs (intramural or near organ)

sections.p: Sympathetic chains run alongside the vertebral column, while parasympathetic ganglia sit near or within target organs. The vagus nerve (CN X) supplies most thoracic and abdominal organs.
b: Sympathetic chain ganglia are adjacent to the aorta and major vessels

sections.p: The sympathetic chain receives arterial blood from the vertebral and intercostal arteries; parasympathetic ganglia are vascularized by branches of the major arteries supplying their target organs.
b: Adequate perfusion is essential for neurotransmitter synthesis

sections.p: Pre‑ganglionic fibers use acetylcholine at nicotinic receptors; post‑ganglionic fibers use norepinephrine (sympathetic) or acetylcholine (parasympathetic).
b: Nicotinic receptors are absent on skeletal muscle end plates

t.b: Elevated in pheochromocytoma; normal in primary orthostatic hypotension
Reduced variability indicates autonomic dysfunction; high variability suggests parasympathetic dominance

sections.p: The ANS maintains homeostasis by adjusting heart rate, vascular tone, airway caliber, digestive motility, and glandular secretion. It operates continuously without conscious input.
b: Sympathetic: increases blood pressure, dilates bronchi
Parasympathetic: slows heart, stimulates gut motility

sections.p: Dysfunction can present as syncope, tachycardia, hypertension, gastroparesis, or autonomic neuropathy. Trauma to the sympathetic chain or vagus nerve can cause severe deficits.

t.b: Positive in pheochromocytoma; negative in essential hypertension
Diagnoses orthostatic hypotension; normal in neurogenic syncope

sections.p: Remember the mnemonic ‘SAD’ for sympathetic: Salivation, Adrenaline, Dilated pupils. Parasympathetic is ‘PRACTICE’: Pupillary constriction, Respiratory rate ↓, Adenylate cyclase ↓, etc.
b: Sympathetic ganglia are located near the spinal cord; parasympathetic ganglia are near organs

whenToSeekHelp: Hypertensive crisis, severe orthostatic hypotension, sudden loss of consciousness, unexplained tachycardia or bradycardia

faq.q: What is the main neurotransmitter of the sympathetic system?
faq.a: Norepinephrine at most effector sites; acetylcholine only at nicotinic ganglionic synapses.

faq.q: Why does the parasympathetic system use acetylcholine everywhere?
faq.a: Acetylcholine is the sole neurotransmitter for parasympathetic pre‑ and post‑ganglionic fibers, acting on muscarinic receptors in target organs.

faq.q: How can I differentiate a sympathetic from a parasympathetic response clinically?
faq.a: Sympathetic: tachycardia, dilated pupils, sweating; parasympathetic: bradycardia, miosis, salivation.
